core_obligations: Record which of the listed properties are general properties of the normalization morphism, citing the corresponding general results (proof lines 8794-8799).

Identify precisely what is not clear from general theory: finiteness of the fibres, finiteness of the induced residue field extensions, and the local description of the normalization as the spectrum of a product of Dedekind domains (proof lines 8800-8803).
Reduce those to the affine, Noetherian, reduced, one-dimensional case, and then to the case where A is a one-dimensional Noetherian domain (proof lines 8804-8809).
Conclude the remaining properties from Krull-Akizuki in the cited form (proof lines 8810-8811).
proof_roadmap: Separate the automatic properties from the ones needing work.
Reduce to the affine reduced case via the description of the normalization.
Reduce further to a one-dimensional Noetherian domain.
Apply Krull-Akizuki in the cited form.
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects six properties of the normalization morphism of a locally Noetherian scheme of dimension one: integrality, surjectivity and bijectivity on components; factorization through the reduction; birationality; the identification of the stalks of the pushforward with integral closures; finiteness of the fibres and of the residue field extensions; and the local description as a finite product of Dedekind domains. The proof observes that most of these are general properties of the normalization but singles out exactly what is not automatic - finiteness of the fibres, finiteness of the residue field extensions and the local Dedekind structure - and reduces those to the affine Noetherian reduced one-dimensional case, then to a one-dimensional Noetherian domain, where the properties follow from Krull-Akizuki (proof lines 8794-8811). H2: the identification of which parts are not covered by general theory and the reduction to the Dedekind case are the substance.
